entities.name: Aetheris
entities.summary:
> The land looks broken on purpose. Roads end in rubble. Towers lean over valleys with no towns left in them. Ruins of five different kinds of kingdom stand on the same hillside, none of them finished, all of them fought over. Wherever you go, somebody's banner flies over somebody else's ruins, and everyone you meet carries a weapon and a grudge.

**What you know**

- Aetheris is a shattered continent of ruins, scavengers, warbands, zealots and conspiracies.
- For as long as anyone can count, the world was remade over and over. A faction would gather the shards of the Ethereal Crystal and rewrite everything. People called it the Cycle of Aetherfalls.
- The Cycle ended about thirty years ago. This is Year 31 Unbound. Nothing resets any more, and history now piles up.
- There are twelve shards. Five great factions still want them.
- Magic and power have a price here: memory, name, blood or sanity.
- The first regular ships have begun crossing the Black Tides to Kaelmar.

| Dominion | Faction | Capital | Lies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The Radiant Ascendancy | Celestial Order | Empyrean Spire | North |
| The Tyrant's Dominion | Crimson Legion | Varkhaal | East |
| The Fractured Nexus | Arcane Consortium | Zepharyos | North-west |
| The Eternal Veil | Shadow Pact | Noctis | West |
| The Verdant Rebirth | Wildborn Clans | The Rootspire | South |

The Hollow Marches sit in the middle, and nobody rules them.

**Getting around**

Each dominion's border is about a week from Hollow Refuge. Each capital is about another week past its border.

**What people say**

- Before the gods there was Fire, and it still burns somewhere.
- The skeletons of gods lie where they fell, at a place called the Titan's Fall.
- There was a war nobody remembers. They call it the Bloodless War.
- A city was stolen from the surface and sunk under the sea.
- The Silent Accord whispers that the Aetherfall was a prison, built by something older than anyone guesses.

entities.name: Ashvale
entities.summary:
> The town hugs the edge of the Rift like it's afraid to let go. Warm air comes up out of the crack and keeps the frost off the nearest roofs. In the middle of town, thirteen standing stones lean together in a ring, older than anything around them. The meeting hall beside them is only half finished, its timbers still raw. Out on the eastern edge, young trees stand in rows with their grafts bound in twine. Somebody near the stones is singing the same four lines over and over.

**What you know**

- Refugees founded Ashvale in 2 AB. They were led by a woman with burned palms, and she wrote the rite the town still keeps.
- Locals say everyone who sleeps in Ashvale is "a hand on the key". Ask them what the key opens and you'll mostly get a shrug.
- Children learn a four-line keeping song. It gets sung at the stones.
- Three groups run things, and they agree the rite must be kept. They don't agree on much else.

| Group | Leader | What they care about |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boundary Keepers | Ritekeeper Orla Hesk | Keeping the rite and the song, sung right. |
| Bloom-Speakers | Master Speaker Tevan Lin | Teaching communion with the Bloom safely, to anyone who asks. Their sanctuary is on the west edge of town. |
| Wrights | Chief Wright Brenna Halvor | Tools that work. They're planting the grafted orchard on the east side. |

**Around town**

- **The east gate** and **the west road** are the ways in and out. The west road crosses a ford.
- **The old waygate** is a ruin under the west road. The Wrights pay for salvage from it.
- **Nine villages** lie in the hills to the west and south: Coldwater, Haskett's Mill, Greyfold, Low Fenn, Oakhallow, Sallow Cross, Kettleby, Brannock and Thornmere.
- **Odran Reeve** trades salt up from Low Fenn.

**What people say**

- No frost ever settles inside the ring of stones.
- Once, years back, the stones were "listening".
- Something still hums down in the old waygate.
- A green gourd-lamp has been showing up at the treeline at night.

sections.heading: Established identity
sections.content:
People of bark, moss, root and fungus. In the first years of the Bloom, the spore-storms rewrote some people into beast-folk. A few they rewrote further, all the way into the Bloom's own grammar. Their descendants are the Bloomborn.

They are people, not the Bloom's moods. They have names, families, grudges and opinions, and they choose for themselves.

**Strengths and flaws:** Patient, hardy and hard to kill. Natural growers and healers. Slow to trust, slower to forget, and they always smell faintly of rain on soil.

sections.heading: Culture and names
sections.content:
Most Bloomborn live in the open Bloom country and the Eastern Deepwood. Many walk with the Spore Circle. Some work Ashvale's orchards beside the Wrights.

Every power in Kaelmar has an opinion about them. Kaelholm studies them with fascination and suspicion. The Convergence Collective calls them proof that the change can be lived. Plenty of ordinary folk just find them restful company.

Bloomborn grow no husk against the Bloom, since they are already part of it. They feel its moods the way others feel weather.

A very few have crossed to Aetheris, where nobody knows what to make of them.

**Common names:** Alder, Bracken, Corrin, Fennick, Hollin, Rue, Sedge, Tansy, Thistle, Wren

sections.heading: D&D adaptation
sections.content: Play a Bloomborn with the firbolg rules from *Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse*, or build one with the custom lineage rules in *Tasha's Cauldron of Everything*. They are Humanoids.

sections.heading: Shared-world relationship

sections.heading: Calendar structure
sections.content:
A single **363-day** year is used on both continents. There are twelve 30-day months grouped into four seasons, plus three festival days outside the months. Weeks have seven days.

| Season | Month 1 | Month 2 | Month 3 | Festival and placement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spring | Spring Dawn | First Seed | Monsoon | Spring Equinox: before Spring Dawn 1; New Year's Day |
| Summer | Midnight Sun | Dry Wind | Harvest | Midsummer: Midnight Sun 15; **not** an extra day |
| Autumn | Fall | Last Seed | Old Winds | Autumn Equinox: before Fall 1 |
| Winter | Snowfall | Evernight | Winter's Dusk | Evernight Festival: between Evernight 30 and Winter's Dusk 1 |

The three extra days are Spring Equinox, Autumn Equinox and Evernight Festival. Midsummer occurs within an existing month and does not increase the year to 364 days.

sections.heading: Date naming
sections.content: Example: `Midnight Sun 15, 300 AB`. Kaelmar counts After Bloom (AB). Aetheris counts Unbound years from the broken Cycle: **300 AB is Year 31 Unbound**, and the stated conversion is Unbound = AB − 269.

entities.name: Empyrean Spire
entities.summary:
*The floating city of white stone where the Celestial Order rules from the Throne of Light.*

> The city hangs in the sky with nothing holding it up. White towers, white walls, white bridges, all of it so bright at noon that pilgrims weep and blame the light. Platforms rise from the plain on chains of gold, loaded with petitioners, soldiers and carts of wheat. At the very top a single spire catches the sun before anything else in the world, and there are no shadows anywhere.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Radiant Ascendancy, and the seat of the Celestial Order.
- The High Theurgists rule from the Throne of Light.
- The Order's chief fortress, the Golden Aerie, stands nearby.
- Order law holds everywhere in the city. Undead, demons and forbidden magic are hunted.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Throne of Light | Where the High Theurgists rule, in a hall with no corners for shadows. Petitioners wait days for an audience. |
| Matins Gate | Platforms drawn up from the plain on golden chains, rising at first light with the morning prayer. The only way up for most. |
| The Narthex | The lowest terraces, where outsiders must stay, like the porch of a temple. Every visitor's name goes into the Pilgrims' Roll. |
| Solenne's Hands | The Order's great infirmary, where its missionary healers train. Over the door: *Mercy within the Law.* |
| The Aureole | Solenne's great temple, on the highest point of the city, where the dawn touches the world first. |
| The Awning | The one inn in the Narthex with a roof that throws shade, which is the whole joke of the name. It serves anyone, and asks no questions out loud. |
| The Glasshouse | The Inquisition's offices, lit so brightly from every side that nobody inside casts a shadow. |
| The Golden Aerie | The Order's chief fortress, on a crag near the city. Radiant knights train there. |

**Who you'll meet**

sections.heading: Established nature
sections.content: Kaelith glyph-work follows a First Grammar: intention wakes resonance; resonance makes a pattern; pattern becomes the world. Kaelith doors listen, and outer gates may demand thirteen notes, a tuning fork, a key or marked blood.

sections.heading: Practice and boundaries
sections.content: Glyph-scars can be carved into flesh, and some spontaneously grow. Everstone does not rot; hatch-metal drives roots away. At the table, this magic uses ordinary 2024 arcane spells where the bible maps them. See the Kaelmar glyph-work rule reference, RUL-302.

> The town looks like it was built out of whatever the last five worlds left lying around. A temple column holds up a tanner's awning. A gatehouse arch that belongs on a palace frames a pig pen. The wall around it all runs in bands of different stone, each one older or newer than the last. Somebody has hung a sign over the nearest door: a bent nail driven through a crown. Inside, people are arguing in three accents, and nobody has reached for a weapon. Here, that counts as peace.

**What you know**

| The Market of Lost Things | Battlefield salvage, old maps, strange coins and objects nobody can name. |
| The Seer's Tower | Home of the Blind Seer. The tower has no windows, because "windows work both ways". |
| The Empty House | Nobody goes in. Nobody can say who lives there. Smoke still rises from the chimney every morning. |
| The Old Wall | Built over centuries, one layer at a time. |
| The East Gate | Where faction envoys come in, and most of the trouble with them. |

**What people say**

- The locals remember things they shouldn't.
- Vara knows metals that shouldn't exist, just by the look of them.
- One stretch of the Old Wall honours a battle nobody in town remembers fighting.
- Ask enough people about the Empty House and every one of them changes the subject.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.content: The change turned back and the world sorted "into its drawers".

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: A scholar corps, monasteries, archives and tribunals of elders in grey. It "burns" offenders by scraping their names off every roll.

sections.heading: Status at 300 AB
sections.content: The strongest power on the continent. It wants every vault opened and catalogued. Led by Archivist-Elder Venn Tull.

sections.heading: Associated people and places
sections.content: Venn Tull

sections.heading: Tensions
sections.content: It seeks to open and catalogue every vault; the Eastern Tendril burns Kaelith work on sight.

entities.name: Kaelholm
entities.summary:
*The grey city of archives and tribunals, Kaelmar's largest, where the ships from Aetheris come in.*

> Grey stone, grey robes, grey sea. The biggest city on the continent climbs up from the harbour in terraces of archives and monasteries, every window lit with somebody reading. Clerks meet every ship at the dock with their ledgers open. Somewhere above, a bell rings, and a name gets struck from the rolls.

**What you know**

- Kaelholm is the largest city on Kaelmar and the first port for ships from Aetheris. It used to be called Kaelith-East.
- It kept Kaelith's name, archives, scholar corps and tribunals. Its elders wear grey.
- It is the strongest power on the continent. It wants every old vault opened and catalogued, and the change turned back so the world goes back "into its drawers".
- Its gnomes are the city's scribes and glyph-wrights.
- Its tribunals can punish someone by scraping their name from every roll. People call it being "burned".
- Glyph-cutting into living flesh is forbidden here.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Tollmouth | The harbour. Every ship, crate and passenger is counted and entered in a ledger before anyone steps ashore. Sailors argue with the clerks in Tidecant. |
| The Sitting | The tribunal halls, where the elders in grey sit in judgement. Locals say "brought before the Sitting". Open to the public, and always full. |
| The Rasp | The hall of rolls, where every name in Kaelholm is kept, and where a burned name is scraped out in front of witnesses. Named for the sound. |
| Vellum House | Home of the Scholar Corps, which trains Kaelholm's scholars and sends out its expeditions. Always hiring guards. |
| Lampblack | The gnome quarter of scribes and glyph-wrights, named for the ink. Its shop signs are written in glyphs that glow faintly after dark. |
| The Fair Copies | Monasteries up on the terraces where everything is copied twice. Some take in travellers, if they can write. |
| The Margin | The night market by the docks, for everything kept out of the ledgers: Aetherian goods off the ships, salt from the south, and worse. |
| The Doused Lamp | A dockside inn for crews off the Black Tides. They keep it dark, out of habit. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Archivist-Elder Venn Tull](/player/e/NPC-308), who heads one of the tribunals.
- Scholars of the Scholar Corps, hiring anyone who can fight.
- Sailors off the Aetheris ships, speaking Tidecant.

**Getting around**

| From Kaelholm to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Eternal Veil's ports, in Aetheris | About two weeks by ship | Across the Black Tides, in the dark. Regular crossings have only just begun. |
| The Eastern Mountains | West, a long road inland | Goliath country, and the Ascendancy's. |
| Ashvale and the Rift | About 1,500 km west | Right across the continent. |

**What people say**

- Venn Tull wants a living Kaelith guardian, and will pay anything to get one.
- The Eastern Tendril of the Spore Circle burns Kaelith work on sight, and Kaelholm's expeditions keep running into them.
- Kaelholm wants to be first to examine anything old that comes off the ships from Aetheris.
- Once you are burned, nobody in the city will say your name aloud.
- The Rasp keeps a second set of rolls, where burned names are never scraped out. Nobody admits to it.

entities.name: Kaelmar
entities.summary:
> Forest grows through everything. Moss on the old stone roads, roots through the walls of towers that were built to last forever. Strange marks glow faintly in the ruins, lines of light that pulse when you get close, as if something is listening. The air smells of loam and spores, and here and there the trees seem to lean toward you.

**What you know**

- Three hundred years ago the Kaelith civilisation tried to move minds between bodies and conquer death. It failed. People call the failure the Shrouding.
- The failure joined spellwork, flesh and forest. The change was paused, not undone, and the Bloom grew through the ruins.
- It's now 300 AB, After Bloom.
- The big question here is who gets to choose what shape another life takes.
- Kaelith glyph-work and the Bloom are two kinds of one magic, a grammar of call and answer. It costs blood, memory or self.
- Under-roads and root paths reach a place people call the between.

| Power | What it wants |
| --- | --- |
| Kaelholm | Every old work catalogued, and the change turned back. |
| The Spore Circle | To tend the Bloom. Its Eastern Tendril burns Kaelith work. |
| The Convergence Collective | The change finished, but only for those who choose it. |
| The Ascendancy | A few minds raised up through the change, and everyone else beneath them. |

**What people say**

- The ruins aren't dead, only sleeping.
- Ships from Aetheris have started arriving at Kaelholm, and everyone wants to know what they're carrying.
- The Bloom remembers everything that happens in it.

sections.heading: Common speech
sections.content:
Common (Aetheris) and Kaelish (Kaelmar) are distant cousin languages. At the table, they may be treated as one language unless the GM deliberately wants the barrier to matter in an adventure. This is the stated flexible convention in the setting bible, not a claim that the languages are identical in-world.

Sailors across the Black Tides mix Common and Kaelish in a trade pidgin called **Tidecant**.

entities.name: Noctis
entities.summary:
*The Shadow Pact's City of Masks, in endless dusk.*

> The sun never quite rises over Noctis, and never quite sets. Everything is purple and grey. Everyone is masked: porcelain, leather, lace, plain black cloth. Streets that led one way this morning lead somewhere else tonight. Music drifts from a hundred doorways. Nobody here uses their real name twice, and nobody asks you for yours.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Eternal Veil, and the seat of the Shadow Pact. Called the City of Masks.
- The rulers meet in the Midnight Court. The Pact's chief fortress, Nightglass, stands nearby.
- Masks are worn everywhere, by everyone. Going unmasked is rude, and unwise.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Midnight Court | Where the Pact's rulers meet behind their masks, and its singers perform. |
| Nightglass | The Pact's chief fortress, just outside the city. Its magistrates judge traitors. |
| Bauta Row | The mask market. Masks are sold, borrowed, stolen and inherited here. Some come with a name attached. |
| The Unlit Door | Ellun's temple: secrets, night and freedom. Its door is never in the same place twice. |
| The Murmur | Where secrets are bought and sold, by the whisper, and nobody sees who is buying. |
| The Alias | An inn where you sign the ledger with someone else's name. Very popular. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Grandmaster Lysander Morrow](/player/e/NPC-044), if he chooses to be met.
- [Ilsevre the Whispering Veil](/player/e/NPC-047), singing at the Midnight Court.
- [Magistrate Renn Varros](/player/e/NPC-053), at Nightglass.
- Merchants and smugglers from both continents, since the ships began crossing.

**Getting around**

| From Noctis to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border, a week through the dusk. |
| The dusk coast and the Black Tides | West | Ships cross to Kaelholm in about two weeks. |
| The Umbral Paths | Everywhere and nowhere | Shifting roads that lead anywhere. |

**What people say**

- Every mask on Bauta Row has been worn before.
- The Grandmaster has been seen in two places on the same night.
- Ask for the same street twice and you will get two different directions, both correct.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Githyanki | Paladin | She/her | The Rift of Unmaking, the Fractured Nexus |

**Looks.** A githyanki warrior priestess with yellow-green skin and a greatsword whose blade is a shaft of solid darkness.

**Manner.** Proud, devout and impatient with doubt.

**Who they are**

- A warrior priestess of the Black Sun, the cult that believes an endless eclipse is coming.
- Carries a sword of darkness.

**What people say**

- When the eclipse comes, Seraine means to be standing in it.

entities.name: Seraphis the Ascended
entities.summary:
*The Order's silent executioner, in white armour that never ages.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unknown | Paladin | They/them | Unknown |

**Looks.** A tall figure in seamless white armour that never dents or tarnishes. Light leaks from the joints. Nobody has seen a face inside, because there may not be one.

**Manner.** Silent. Communicates by pointing, and by what happens next.

**Who they are**

- The Celestial Order's silent executioner, in [The Radiant Ascendancy](/player/e/REG-002).
- Wears armour that never seems to age.

**What people say**

- Seraphis may once have been mortal.
- Nobody has heard Seraphis speak.
- The light from the armour is warm. Those who have stood close enough say it feels like forgiveness.

sections.heading: Established identity
sections.content:
Born from an erased past, living between light and dark.

**Strengths and flaws as described by the cards:** Masters of stealth. Distrusted everywhere.

entities.name: Sirala "the Deep Mourner"
entities.summary:
*A sea elf whose song calls the drowned home.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sea Elf | Cleric | She/her | The waters under the Black Tides, she says |

**Looks.** A sea elf with grey-green skin, dressed in black mourning lace that floats around her even on land.

**Manner.** Soft, grieving and endlessly patient.

**Who they are**

- A singer of the Drowned Saints.

**What people say**

- Her song calls the drowned home.

entities.name: Sister Elyra Vale
entities.summary:
*The youngest Vale: an Order healer who treats anyone bleeding.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human | Cleric | She/her | Ashen Spire, the Hollow Marches |

**Looks.** A young woman with the Vale family's grey eyes, sleeves always rolled up, and a healer's satchel stitched with the Order's sun.

**Manner.** Warm, earnest and stubborn. Treats anyone who is bleeding, whatever their colours.

**Who they are**

- A Celestial Order healer in [The Hollow Marches](/player/e/REG-001), often at the Lantern House in [Hollow Refuge](/player/e/SET-001).
- Youngest of the Vale family of Ashen Spire. Sister to [Brother Altharion Vale](/player/e/NPC-020), [Tobias Vale](/player/e/NPC-051) and [Professor Orin Vale](/player/e/NPC-007).

**What people say**

- She treats anyone who is bleeding, whatever their colours.
- Some in the Order call her soft. Nobody says it twice in the Lantern House.
- She writes long letters every night. Nobody knows to whom.

entities.name: Sister Kallisa "the Pyre-Singer"
entities.summary:
*An aarakocra singer whose hymns raise infernos.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aarakocra | Bard | She/her | A village burned by the Legion |

**Looks.** A tall aarakocra with scorched red-black feathers at her throat and a voice that carries over any fire.

**Manner.** Joyful, gentle and terrifying when she sings.

**Who they are**

- A singer of the Ashen Covenant.

**What people say**

- Her hymns raise infernos.
- The burning sing along.

entities.name: Sorcerer-King Jorvas Myrr
entities.summary:
*A triton king who gave up his throne for storm magic.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Triton | Mage | He/him | An undersea kingdom off the dusk coast |

**Looks.** A triton with blue-green skin and a crown of grey coral he still wears out of habit. Static crackles in his hair.

**Manner.** Regal, wistful and a little bored by everyone.

**Who they are**

- A mage of the Arcane Consortium, in [The Fractured Nexus](/player/e/REG-004).
- Once a king. Gave up the throne for storm magic.

**What people say**

- Myrr thinks it was a fair trade.
- His old subjects still send envoys. He never receives them.

- He is collecting storm reports from every dominion.

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: Drilled columns, siege constructs and soldiers remade with iron and graft.

sections.content: Dace Corvane

entities.name: The Ash Barrens
entities.summary:
> Grey ash under grey sky. The wind lifts it in sheets and lays it down again somewhere else. Herds move across the plain in long lines, driven by orc riders who know every dip and ridge by heart. There's no water you'd want to drink, and no shade at all.

**What you know**

- The ash barrens lie east of central Kaelmar.
- Orc herders live there.

**What people say**

- The herders don't say what burned here. Ask, and they change the subject.
- The ash is deeper than any well anyone's dug.

entities.name: The Ashen Wastes
entities.summary:
> The ground is warm through your boots. Ash drifts like snow and never settles. The charred bones of a city stand on the skyline, towers burned hollow, and between them the horizon glows orange at noon and midnight alike. Somewhere out there, something is still burning, and it has been burning longer than anyone remembers.

**What you know**

- A burned empire where the fire never dies.
- The myths say that before the gods there was Fire, and the first flame still burns here without fuel.
- Nobody agrees on exactly where it is.

**What people say**

- Some call the First Fire creation's source. Others say it's what will be left at the end.
- The Ashen Covenant believes the world must burn to be reborn, and they're searching the Wastes for the First Fire.
- The empire didn't burn because of a war. It burned because someone found the Fire.

entities.name: The Black Tides
entities.summary:
> The sea is black and flat and swallows every light. No moon on the water, no stars. The crew talks in whispers in a jumble of two languages. At dusk the captain orders every lantern doused, and nobody argues. Below the keel, the water goes down further than anyone wants to think about.

**What you know**

- A sunless sea between Aetheris and Kaelmar.
- Ships cross between Kaelholm and the ports of the Eternal Veil. The crossing takes about two weeks in the dark. Regular crossings have only just begun.
- Crews light no lanterns over the trench.
- Sailors speak Tidecant, a pidgin of Common and Kaelish.

**What people say**

- A trench runs under the sea, and that's why it's dark.
- In Aetheris some say the Tides lead to another world.
- Smugglers move people across who don't want to be found.
- The Drowned Saints say a city lies sunk beneath these waters, waiting to rise.

entities.name: The Blind Seer
entities.summary:
*The blind Taur'n prophet of Hollow Refuge, in his windowless tower.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Taur'n | Mystic | He/him | Nobody knows |

**Looks.** A huge, stooped Taur'n with rune-marked horns worn smooth, and two white scars where his eyes were. He never seems to bump into anything.

**Manner.** Unhurried and kind, with a habit of answering the question you were about to ask.

**Who they are**

- The prophet of [Hollow Refuge](/player/e/SET-001).
- Lives in the Seer's Tower, which has no windows, because "windows work both ways".
- Put out his own eyes to see the Eternal Eclipse.

**What people say**

- People climb the tower for advice and come down quieter.
- He answers the question you were about to ask.
- He is older than the Refuge.

entities.name: The Bloodmarked Fields
entities.summary:
> The grass gives up a mile out. After that it's mud the colour of old rust, cut by trenches nobody bothered to fill and stakes nobody bothered to pull. Crows work the ground in no hurry at all. Five sets of colours fly over five dug-in lines, close enough to shout insults across. Somewhere in the middle, a work crew is digging, and every line is watching them.

**What you know**

- Every faction fights here, and the fighting is over shards. They keep surfacing in this ground.
- It's half a day from Hollow Refuge, and the road is risky.
- From the Fields it's half a day to the Scar, or a full day to Wither's Hollow. Both roads are dangerous.
- Nobody holds the Fields for long.

**What people say**

- Every faction has sent somebody new this season. Something has them stirred up.
- The digging isn't about salvage. Somebody thinks there's something big under there.
- Whoever walks off the Fields with a shard won't be left alone afterwards.

entities.name: The Bloodmoon Spire
entities.summary:
> The moon comes up red, and the mist on the moor starts to move. When it thins, a tower stands where there was nothing an hour ago, black against the red light, with one window lit at the very top. By dawn it's gone, and the grass where it stood isn't even flattened.

**What you know**

- A tower that rises from the mist only when the moon turns red.
- Nobody agrees on where it is.

**What people say**

- Whoever goes in has until the moon turns pale again to get out.
- The Black Sun cult watches for red moons. They believe an endless eclipse is coming, and that something older than the gods will come out of it.
- The light in the top window is always lit.

sections.heading: Established nature
sections.content: The Bloom is a weather of minds in the mycelium, not a single speaking mind. It thinks by pulse and growth. Communion opens a person to it, at a cost in self; those who go too deep may cease to know where they end.

sections.heading: Practice and boundaries
sections.content: Spore-bound people listen through roots, read memories in old mycelia, grow living houses and heal with membranes that remember the body’s intended form. The membranes cannot take iron. Adaptive spores permit temporary passage through hostile Bloom. The Bloom drank Kaelith constructs and learned from them; circuit-roots and Arbors followed.

entities.name: The Bloom Cathedral
entities.summary:
> The tunnel opens into a hall. Roots rise like columns to a ceiling you can't see, twisting in slow spirals. The light is green and soft and seems to come from everywhere. There's no door on the far side, only a wall of roots, and the longer you stand here the more certain you are that the hall is waiting for you to say something.

**What you know**

- A tunnel junction under Kaelmar, grown into a hall of root columns and slow spirals.
- You have to ask it for passage.

**What people say**

- What you have to pay to pass depends on what you're carrying.
- The Bloom-Speakers can talk to it. Some people say it talks back.

entities.name: The Cantor
entities.summary:
*The erased leader of the Nameless Choir, who cannot keep a name.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eladrin | Bard | She/her | Erased |

**Looks.** A winter eladrin whose face slides out of memory the moment you look away. People remember her voice, and frost, and nothing else.

**Manner.** Gentle and sorrowful. Hums when she is not speaking.

**Who they are**

- Leader of the Nameless Choir, people erased from history who want to learn who took their names.

**What people say**

- She was erased from history long ago.
- She chose a title because she cannot keep a name.
- The Choir sings songs nobody remembers hearing.

entities.name: The Central Bloom Country
entities.summary:
> The ground gives slightly underfoot. The Bloom has covered everything: hills, ruins and old roads, all under a soft carpet of moss and fungus that glows faintly at dusk. Here and there a stairway leads down into the earth, its walls lit with old glyphs. The whole country seems to be breathing.

**What you know**

- Open Bloom country covers the centre of Kaelmar.
- The under-roads run beneath it.
- The Bloom-Speakers of Ashvale teach how to commune with the Bloom safely.

**What people say**

- The Bloom answers when it's spoken to properly. The trouble is knowing what it will ask in return.
- There are more ways down to the under-roads than anyone has mapped.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.content: The change finished as first intended, chosen and never forced.

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: A faith with Root Texts, elders and "cycles". Its Warband rides half-living constructs. Members are cut with glyphs and grafts.

sections.heading: Status at 300 AB
sections.content: A young faith. Its first Riftwalker, Maro Grane, is still writing the Root Texts.

sections.heading: Associated people and places
sections.content: [Maro Grane](/player/e/NPC-310)

sections.heading: Tensions
sections.content: It rejects the Ascendancy’s hierarchy and argues that the change must be freely chosen.

entities.name: The Eastern Deepwood
entities.summary:
> The forest and the ruins have grown into one thing. Ferns with copper veins brush your knees. Towers rise out of the canopy, furred with fungus from top to bottom. The rot on the fallen logs moves when you're not looking straight at it. Then the air goes still, and the spores start to drift.

**What you know**

- Forest and Kaelith ruins grown together, in eastern Kaelmar.
- Copper-veined ferns, fungus-covered towers, thinking rot and spore-storms.
- Thornhaven, the seat of the Spore Circle's Eastern Tendril, is here, and so is the Survey Garden.

**What people say**

- The rot thinks. Some say it remembers too.
- Get caught in a spore-storm and you might not come out the same person.
- Kaelholm sends expeditions in. The Eastern Tendril burns what they find.

entities.name: The Eastern Mountains
entities.summary:
> The Deepwood thins out into scree, and the mountains rise ahead, grey and white. Goliath herders watch you climb from the ridges and don't wave. Further up, you pass a camp where soldiers drill in columns, and half of them carry iron grafted onto their bodies.

**What you know**

- Mountain country east of the Deepwood.
- Goliath clans live here.
- The Ascendancy began here, as a doctrine inside a mercenary legion. It's not an army yet.
- Marshal Dace Corvane leads it, a hobgoblin mercenary captain who "keeps the count".

**What people say**

- The Ascendancy is searching these mountains for a lost Kaelith vault.
- Corvane wants an army, and sounds very reasonable when explaining why.
- The Ascendancy's soldiers are remade with iron and graft.

entities.name: The Eternal Veil
entities.summary:
> The sun never quite rises here, and never quite sets. Dusk hangs over everything, purple and grey. In Noctis everyone wears a mask, and nobody uses their real name twice. Streets that led one way this morning lead somewhere else tonight. Past the last harbour lies the Black Tides, flat and dark as ink, and no light comes off it at all.

**What you know**

- This is the dominion of the Shadow Pact. Its creed: rule unseen, and truth is whatever is believed. Its emblem is a broken black circle.
- The Pact promises freedom from any permanent central control. It wants perpetual twilight, where identities shift, histories get rewritten and assassins run the cities.
- The capital is Noctis, the City of Masks, in endless dusk. The rulers meet in the Midnight Court. The chief fortress is Nightglass.
- The Pact's leaders are Grandmaster Lysander Morrow and Spymaster Tobias Vale.
- Its forces are Silent Blades, illusionists, Shadow Lashers and executioners.
- Ships cross from the Veil's ports to Kaelholm in Kaelmar. Regular crossings have only just begun.

**Places**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Umbral Paths | Shifting roads that lead anywhere. |
| The Veilborn Archive | A hall of stone masks. |
| The Black Tides | A sunless sea. |

The other four factions keep enclaves here: the Last Beacon (Order), the Bleeding Arena (Legion), the Woven Sanctum (Consortium) and the Fading Grove (Wildborn).

**Getting around**

The border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and Noctis is about another week beyond it. The crossing to Kaelmar takes about two weeks.

**What people say**

- Rivals say the Pact fights control by controlling everything in secret.
- Every mask in the Veilborn Archive belonged to somebody.
- The Umbral Paths will take you anywhere, but not always where you asked.
- The Drowned Saints preach on the docks that a sunken city will rise and the sea will take back what was stolen.

entities.name: The Fractured Nexus
entities.summary:
> The sky up here is wrong. Storms move against the wind. Islands of rock drift overhead, trailing roots and waterfalls that never reach the ground. Lightning hangs in the air a heartbeat too long. Somewhere above the clouds, a city of towers turns slowly, and the air tastes of metal and burnt paper.

**What you know**

- This is the dominion of the Arcane Consortium. Its creed: reality is a puzzle to be rewritten. Its emblem is a violet geometric eye, or a prism.
- The Consortium promises a world no longer held back by ignorance. It wants limitless magic: floating islands, shifting time, cities that move between dimensions.
- The capital is Zepharyos, City of the Unbound, among the clouds. The council sits in the Nexus Spire. The chief fortress is the Nexus Collegium.
- The Consortium's leaders are Archmagister Veylan Orithis and Archivist Lissara Wynne.
- Its forces are scholars, constructs, dimensional mercenaries and Eye Beasts.

**Places**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Rift of Unmaking | An elemental vortex. |
| The Echoing Halls | A labyrinth of mirrors. |
| The Repository of the Unwritten | A forbidden vault. |

The other four factions keep enclaves here: the Last Unbroken Chapel (Order), the Warbound Coliseum (Legion), the Veilfracture (Pact) and the Living Wilds (Wildborn).

**Getting around**

The border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and Zepharyos is about another week beyond it. The high country is all storms and floating rock.

**What people say**

- Archmagister Orithis is one experiment away from going too far.
- Nobody has ever seen the true face of Lord Varkoss, the illusionist. Some say Varkoss doesn't exist at all.
- The Consortium treats catastrophe as the cost of research.
- What goes into the Repository of the Unwritten doesn't come out.

entities.name: The Hollow Marches
entities.summary:
> The road gives out before the land does. Past the last milestone the ground turns to churned clay and old iron, a rusted helm here, a spear shaft gone grey there, all of it half swallowed by the grass. Ruins stand on every rise. None of them match. A Legion banner snaps over one ridge, and on the next a column of white smoke climbs from somebody else's camp. Nobody owns this country. Everybody is trying to.

**What you know**

- The Marches are the heartland of Aetheris. Forgotten kingdoms once met here.
- All five dominions border it, and none of them rules it. The Celestial Order, the Crimson Legion, the Arcane Consortium, the Shadow Pact and the Wildborn Clans all keep camps and send patrols.
- Hollow Refuge is the one neutral town. Most travel starts there.
- Ashen Spire was the capital of the last kingdom. It's a ruin now, picked over by scavengers and sellswords.
- The Scar is a battlefield of rusted steel that never ends.
- Blackveil Fortress is an abandoned stronghold. People who go into its depths don't come back.
- The Sunken Archive is a library under the ground, laid out like a maze.
- Wither's Hollow is a dead forest, always in mist.
- The Cairn of the Forgotten is a field of graves with no names on them.

**Getting around**

| From Hollow Refuge to | Time | How safe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Crossroads of Fate | Half a day | Watched, usually safe |
| The Bloodmarked Fields | Half a day | Risky |
| Blackveil Fortress | 1 day | Risky |

Past those three, the roads get worse. The routes out to the Rift are openly hostile.

**What people say**

- The dead on the Scar don't stay down.
- Read too long in the Sunken Archive and you start remembering things that were never yours.
- The paths in Wither's Hollow move once you've walked past them.
- Some of the nameless graves at the Cairn stir.
- Restless spirits still walk Ashen Spire.

entities.name: The Hollowed Veil
entities.summary:
> The birds stop first. Then the wind. A leaf hangs in the air beside you and doesn't fall. People walk past in the mist, in clothes a hundred years out of fashion, and none of them look at you. One of them is calling a name, over and over, the same way each time.

**What you know**

- A place where time forgets to move and the lost still walk.
- Nobody agrees on where it is.

**What people say**

- Stay too long and you'll walk out to find everyone you knew has grown old.
- The lost aren't ghosts. They're people who walked in and haven't noticed yet.
- The Nameless, people erased from history, look for their names here.

entities.name: The Layout of the World
entities.summary:
> Lay the world out east to west and it reads like a sentence. Aetheris. The Eternal Veil's dusk coast. The Black Tides. Kaelholm on the far shore. Then Kaelmar, running west to the Rift.

**What you know**

| In Aetheris | What lies there |
| --- | --- |
| Centre | The Hollow Marches, the lawless heartland. Every dominion borders it. |
| North | The Radiant Ascendancy: golden plains up to the Luminara Gate. |
| North-west | The Fractured Nexus: high country of storms and floating rock. |
| East | The Tyrant's Dominion: iron mountains, with the Bloodfields facing the Marches. |
| South | The Verdant Rebirth: roadless forest. |
| West | The Eternal Veil: a dusk coast on the Black Tides. |

| In Kaelmar | What lies there |
| --- | --- |
| North-west | The Rift, with Ashvale on its lip and nine villages in the hills. |
| Centre | Open Bloom country over the under-roads. |
| East of centre | The ash barrens, where orcs herd. |
| East | The Eastern Deepwood, then the eastern mountains. |
| Far east | Kaelholm, then the coast and the Black Tides. |
| North | Cold highlands and ice. |
| South | Fens, lakes and river country. |

**Getting around**

- In Aetheris, each dominion's border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and each capital about another week beyond.
- Kaelmar is about 1,500 km from the Rift to the east coast.
- The crossing between the continents takes about two weeks by ship.

**What people say**

- Nobody has mapped the far shores of either continent.
- The Rift runs under all of it.

entities.name: The Luminara Gate
entities.summary:
> The plains end in light. An arch stands alone against the sky, bright enough to make your eyes water, with nothing behind it but more light. The air hums. Pilgrims kneel in rows before it, and not one of them goes through.

**What you know**

- An arch of light in the Radiant Ascendancy, in the far north.
- People say it stands at the edge of the world.

**What people say**

- Nobody who's walked through has come back to say what's on the other side.
- The Celestial Order guards it. Whether it keeps people in or out depends who you ask.
- It isn't the edge of the world. It's a door.

sections.heading: Established lore
sections.content:
| Age | What the cards say |
| --- | --- |
| Before the gods | There was Fire. The first flame still burns without fuel in [the Ashen Wastes](/player/e/LOC-004). Some call it creation's source, others what remains at the end. |
| The whole world | One world existed, unbroken and eternal. |
| The Shattering | The Elders broke the Ethereal Crystal. See COS-902. |
| The age of gods | Gods fought at the Titan's Fall, and their colossal skeletons still lie there. Their weapons were made at the Nameless Forge. One god tried to sit the Shattered Throne and failed. |
| The Cycle | Again and again a faction gathered the shards and remade the world. The Hidden Ones guided each turn and erased whoever came too close to the truth. |
| Things erased | A war nobody remembers: the Bloodless War. A king who tried to seize the Loom: the Unraveled King. A city stolen from the surface and sunk: the Drowned City. Someone who tried to break the Aetherfall and was unmade. |
| The Broken World | The last great kingdom fell. Its capital, Ashen Spire, is a ruin. The shards were lost again, and no faction holds power. |

entities.name: The Northern Highlands and Ice
entities.summary:
> The wind comes down off the ice and doesn't stop. The highlands are bare rock and frozen moss, and the only shelter is in the dwarf-halls cut into the mountainsides, their doors so well hidden you'd walk right past them. Further north, the ice runs to the end of sight.

**What you know**

- Cold highlands and ice cover northern Kaelmar.
- Dwarves hold the highlands.

**What people say**

- The dwarves have been guarding something in the mountains for longer than they'll admit.
- Out on the ice, sometimes, there are lights under the surface.

entities.name: The Radiant Ascendancy
entities.summary:
> The plains run gold to the horizon, wheat or grass or something brighter, it's hard to tell in this light. Shrines stand at every crossroads, scrubbed white. Far to the north, a city of white stone hangs in the sky with nothing holding it up. Patrols in polished armour ride past and look at you a moment too long, as if they're counting your sins.

**What you know**

- This is the dominion of the Celestial Order. Its creed is divine rule, purity and absolute law. Its emblem is a rising golden sun.
- The Order promises peace through enlightened order. It wants a golden theocracy under a sun that never sets, with undead, demons and forbidden magic wiped out. Its enemies say dissent gets wiped out too.
- The capital is Empyrean Spire, a floating city of white stone. The High Theurgists rule from the Throne of Light. The Order's chief fortress, the Golden Aerie, stands nearby.
- The Order's leaders are Highlord Theos Valcairn, Grand Theurgist Selara Dawnveil and Inquisitor Malrik Vael.
- Its forces are radiant knights, inquisitors, seraphs and missionary healers.

**Places**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Radiant Expanse | Golden plains. |
| The Luminara Gate | An arch of light, said to stand at the world's edge. |
| The Purged Halls | A city erased for rebellion. |

The other four factions keep enclaves here: Bastion of the Unbroken (Legion), the Sanctum of the Everseeing (Consortium), the Eclipsed Chamber (Pact) and the Thornward Grove (Wildborn).

**Getting around**

The border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and Empyrean Spire is about another week beyond it.

**What people say**

- The Order calls obedience "harmony".
- Highlord Valcairn once doubted the Order. Nobody says so twice within the Highlord's hearing.
- The Thornward Grove is tolerated as a shrine to Solenne, but its keepers are hiding Wildborn who fled the Order.
- Nobody lives in the Purged Halls, but lamps still get lit there.

entities.name: The Rift
entities.summary:
The Rift opens in two places, one on each continent. Use the read-aloud text for whichever one the party reaches.

**In the Hollow Marches (Aetheris)**

> You hear it before you see it, a low hum you feel in your back teeth. Then the ground stops. The chasm runs off in both directions further than you can see, and there's no bottom to it. Drop a stone and you'll be waiting a long time. The air at the edge tastes of copper and tin, and the hair on your arms won't lie down.

**At Ashvale (Kaelmar)**

> It's a crack in the world. It runs out of sight both ways, and warm air breathes up out of it, steady as a sleeper's breath, even on a frost morning. Fungus glows along the lip in pale greens and blues. Between the glowing patches there's a mold you keep catching from the corner of your eye. You'd swear it's watching you.

**What you know**

- The eastern Rift sits at the far edge of the Hollow Marches. Every road there is openly hostile. It's a day from Blackveil Fortress, or half a day from the Sunken Archive or Wither's Hollow.
- The western Rift runs beside Ashvale. The town is built right on its lip.
- Ashvale's ring of thirteen standing stones stands close to the edge.

**What people say**

- In Aetheris: the Rift has something to do with how the Aetherfall began.
- Mother Thorn, a Wildborn elder, is afraid of "what the land remembers beneath the Rift".
- In Kaelmar, the Convergence Collective has its own Riftwalker, Maro Grane.
- Scholars and a few drunk sailors say the two openings are one wound. It runs under the land and drops into a trench under the Black Tides, and that's why that sea has no light.
- Somebody from Aetheris has been drawing maps of the Rift.

entities.name: The Rift of Echoes
entities.summary:
> You hear your own voice before you speak. Then you hear it again, older. The ground ahead drops away into a haze where shapes move: a battle, a wedding, a fire, a city that isn't built yet. Somebody down there turns and looks right at you, and they have your face.

**What you know**

- People call it the edge of Aetheris, where past, present and future collide.
- Nobody agrees on whether it is truly the edge of anything.

**What people say**

- The Whispering Circle says time loops, and their seers don't predict the future, they remember it. Some say they learned it here.
- What you see in the haze has already happened, or will.
- Don't answer if the echo calls your name.

entities.name: The Rootspire
entities.summary:
*The Wildborn Clans' colossal tree-city, grown over the bones of a ruined capital.*

> The tree is the size of a mountain. Its roots have swallowed a whole city, and you can still see the old streets down there, stone arches and towers lifted into the air in the grip of living wood. Houses hang from the branches like fruit. Rope bridges sway between them. Wolves pad along the lower roots, and somewhere far above, a horn sounds.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Verdant Rebirth, and the home of the Wildborn Clans. A colossal tree-city over a ruined capital.
- The elders meet at the Den of Elders. The Clans' chief fortress, the Verdant Crown, stands nearby.
- There are no roads in the Verdant Rebirth. The way here is through the forest.
- Outsiders are welcome if they behave.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Den of Elders | Where the clan elders meet, in a hollow deep in the trunk. No chairs, no thrones, no table head. |
| Old Crown | The old capital's streets and towers, lifted inside the roots. The Wildborn will not say its real name. Some of it is still lived in. |
| The Bough | The market, slung from the branches: furs, herbs, carvings, and very fresh meat. |
| Antler Hollow | Orrowen's shrine: the wild, the seasons and beasts. Offerings are left for whatever comes to take them. |
| The Howl | The lower roots, where the wolf packs den. Visitors walk quickly. |
| The Bare Ground | A patch deep in Old Crown where the roots have never grown. |
| The Verdant Crown | The Clans' chief fortress, a short climb away. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [High Shaman Raethan "Stormcaller"](/player/e/NPC-054) and [Elder Myrris Thornveil](/player/e/NPC-060), at the Den of Elders.
- [Brynn Wolfsong](/player/e/NPC-062), with the wolves.
- [Faelyn Moondancer](/player/e/NPC-056) and [Ogrim Ironhide](/player/e/NPC-059), when they are home.

**Getting around**

| From the Rootspire to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border, a week through roadless forest. |
| Fangholt and the Ravaged Pass | Elsewhere in the Verdant Rebirth | A behemoth's skeleton, and a haunted canyon. |

**What people say**

- The tree is still growing, and is slowly lifting the old city's bones into the air.
- Leave your axe at the roots, or the tree will remember.
- The old capital's last king lies under the Bare Ground, and the tree will not touch him.

entities.name: The Southern Fens, Lakes and River Country
entities.summary:
> The land goes soft and wet and full of birds. Reed beds stretch away into mist, cut by slow green channels. Flat-bottomed boats pass loaded with goods, halfling traders calling prices to each other across the water. Out in the deep fen, something large and slow surfaces, and a tortle on its shell-back raises a hand to you.

**What you know**

- Southern Kaelmar is fens, lakes and river country.
- Halfling traders work the waterways.
- Tortles and lizardfolk keep the fens.

**What people say**

- The halflings know every channel, and will take you anywhere if the price is right.
- Some of the lakes are deeper than they ought to be.
- The fen-keepers say the water remembers.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.content: To tend the conversation between people and the Bloom.

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: Druids bound by communion, ranked in Tendrils. The Sixth Tendril goes deepest. The Eastern Tendril burns Kaelith work and carries lamps grown in gourds.

sections.heading: Status at 300 AB
sections.content: Well established. Its oldest elves saw the Shrouding as children. Elder Sorrel leads the Eastern Tendril.

sections.heading: Associated people and places
sections.content: [Elder Sorrel](/player/e/NPC-307)

sections.heading: Tensions
sections.content: Its Eastern Tendril opposes Kaelholm’s vault expeditions.

entities.name: The Survey Garden
entities.summary:
> Rows of glass houses, all of them broken, and the plants have long since climbed out. Labels in old Kaelith script still hang from stakes, over things that have grown into something else. As you walk, the leaves turn to follow you, and you have the feeling you're being written down.

**What you know**

- An abandoned Kaelith herbarium, overgrown by its own test plots, in the Eastern Deepwood.
- Its plants record what passes them.

**What people say**

- Kaelholm would pay well for anyone who can read what the plants have recorded.
- Some of the old labels describe plants that haven't grown yet.

entities.name: The Tyrant's Dominion
entities.summary:
> Iron mountains, black and red, and every pass guarded by a fort. You hear the crowds at Varkhaal before you see the walls, a roar that rises and breaks and rises again from the Great Arena. Out here every dispute is a duel, and every village has a fighting pit. The smiths never stop. Some of the smoke rises out of the mountainsides themselves.

**What you know**

- This is the dominion of the Crimson Legion. Its creed: only the strong deserve to rule. Its emblem is a crimson blade or a clenched fist.
- The Legion promises strength that can survive anything. It wants endless war: every settlement a fortress, every dispute a duel, an arena in every city.
- The capital is Varkhaal, the Iron Citadel, with its Great Arena. Warlords meet in the Warlord's Hall. The chief fortress is the Red Bastion.
- The Legion's leaders are Warlord Garron Kael and General Orana Volkash.
- Its forces are Shock Troopers, Centurions, Scouts, gladiators and siege companies.

**Places**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Bloodfields | A permanent warfront on the border facing the Hollow Marches. |
| The Ruins of the Old Kings | What's left of older rulers. |
| The Anvil of Dominion | War-forges under the mountains. |

The other four factions keep enclaves here: the Last Sanctuary (Order), the Ember Archives (Consortium), the Hollow Blades' Den (Pact) and the Bloodfang Warcamp (Wildborn).

**Getting around**

The border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and Varkhaal is about another week beyond it.

**What people say**

- Garron Kael rules from the battlefield, not the throne, through sheer brutality.
- Rivals say the Legion's "strength" just means whatever helps the Legion.
- The forges under the Anvil are older than the Legion.
- The Bloodbound Company, a mercenary brotherhood, recruits at the arenas. Blood is the only coin they trust.

entities.name: The Under-Roads
entities.summary:
> The tunnel walls glow with glyphs, line after line, brightening as you pass and fading behind you. Rails run along the floor for sleds that haven't moved in three hundred years. Roots as thick as pillars hold up the ceiling, and some of them pulse faintly, like something is moving through them.

**What you know**

- Ancient tunnels, lit by glyphs, run under Kaelmar and link the thirteen old vaults.
- Rune-sleds used to run through them. Circuit-roots hold up many of the galleries.
- At one tunnel junction stands the Bloom Cathedral, which must be asked for passage.
- At a rot crossroads, the roots can carry travellers through the between, for a price.

**What people say**

- Some sleds still run, with nobody aboard.
- The roots will take you anywhere, but they always take something too.
- Kaelholm has mapped some of the under-roads. It hasn't shared the maps.

entities.name: The Verdant Rebirth
entities.summary:
> There are no roads. The forest closes behind you like a door. Roots as thick as houses climb over the bones of buildings, and moss has swallowed whole streets. Somewhere ahead a tree the size of a mountain rises out of a ruined city, and lights move in its branches. Something big is following you, quietly, just out of sight.

**What you know**

- This is the dominion of the Wildborn Clans. Their creed: civilisation is a disease. Their emblem is a green crown of roots.
- The Clans promise a world that can go on living. They want cities swallowed by forest, no kings, weaker magic and the law of the wild.
- The capital is the Rootspire, a colossal tree-city grown over a ruined capital. The elders meet at the Den of Elders. The chief fortress is the Verdant Crown.
- The Clans' leaders are High Shaman Raethan Stormcaller and Elder Myrris Thornveil.
- Their forces are beast hunters, shamans, primal spirits and living constructs of root and bone.

**Places**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Green Expanse | Roadless wilds. |
| Fangholt | The skeleton of a behemoth. |
| The Ravaged Pass | A haunted canyon. |

The other four factions keep enclaves here: the Hollow Shrine (Order), the Bloodfang Pit (Legion), the Verdant Sanctum (Consortium) and the Hollow Grove (Pact).

**Getting around**

The border is about a week from Hollow Refuge, and the Rootspire is about another week beyond it. There are no roads.

**What people say**

- Raethan Stormcaller, a towering lizardfolk shaman, commands storms and beasts.
- Rivals say the Clans would sacrifice a city to save a tree.
- Nobody knows what killed the behemoth at Fangholt.
- Travellers who camp in the Ravaged Pass hear an army marching all night.

entities.name: The World
entities.summary:
> Unroll the map. Two continents, one sea between them. On the east, Aetheris, broken into five dominions around a lawless middle. On the west, Kaelmar, where forest and old spellwork have grown together. Between them, the Black Tides, black on every copy of this map, because nobody has ever drawn what's under them.

**What you know**

- One world, two continents: Aetheris in the east and Kaelmar in the west. The Black Tides, a sunless sea, lie between them.
- Both continents worship the same gods, use the same coin and share much of their language.
- It's 300 After Bloom (AB) in Kaelmar and Year 31 Unbound in Aetheris. It's the same year.
- The year has 363 days: twelve 30-day months, plus three festival days that belong to no month.
- Ships cross the Black Tides between Kaelholm and the Eternal Veil in about two weeks.

**The gods**

| God | Portfolio |
| --- | --- |
| Solenne, the Dawn Mother | Light, law and mercy |
| Karrath, the Red Victor | War, strength and sworn oaths |
| Ithiel, the Many-Eyed | Knowledge, magic and the stars |
| Ellun, the Maskwright | Secrets, night and freedom |
| Orrowen, the Green Antler | The wild, the seasons and beasts |
| Sephane, Keeper of the Cairn | Death, memory and names |

Three gods are dead: Maruun the Sundered Tide, Aurex the Throne-Breaker and the Nameless Smith.

**What people say**

- The gods are real and answer prayers, but ask a priest about the Cycle and you'll get nothing.
- The Rift opens on both continents. Some say it's one wound, and that the two ends meet somewhere in between.
- In Kaelmar, the roots under the ground lead to the same place.

sections.content: Tools that work.

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: Ashvale's artisans, called Technologists in the novel. They make warding stones, listening bowls, walkers and grafted orchards.

sections.heading: Status at 300 AB
sections.content: Led by Chief Wright Brenna Halvor.

sections.heading: Associated people and places
sections.content: Brenna Halvor

sections.content: They need usable salvage from the waygate while other factions fear waking old work.

entities.name: The founder
entities.summary:
*The nameless woman with burned palms who founded Ashvale.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human | Unknown | She/her | Unknown |

**Looks.** Remembered as a small woman with burned palms. Ashvale's children draw her with her hands held up.

**Manner.** In the stories: blunt, tired and kind.

**Who they are**

- The woman with burned palms who led refugees to found [Ashvale](/player/e/SET-301) in 2 AB.
- Wrote the rite the town still keeps.
- Died about 250 years ago. Nobody remembers her name.

**What people say**

- Ashvale's children draw her with her hands held up.
- She is buried near the stones.
- Her burns never healed.

entities.name: Thornhaven
entities.summary:
> Lamps hang in the branches, green light glowing through the skins of hollowed gourds. Smoke rises from a pit where something carved and glowing is being burned, and the people around it watch until it's ash. Nobody here carries anything made by the Kaelith. They check your pack before they let you sit down.

**What you know**

- Thornhaven is the seat of the Spore Circle's Eastern Tendril, in the Eastern Deepwood.
- The Eastern Tendril burns Kaelith work and carries lamps grown in gourds.
- Elder Sorrel leads it, an elf of about 320 who saw the Shrouding as a child.
- The Tendril opposes Kaelholm's expeditions into the old vaults.

**What people say**

- Elder Sorrel wants every piece of Kaelith work burned, and will never forgive what happened.
- The gourd-lamps don't need oil.
- Tendril scouts have been seen a long way from the Deepwood, carrying green lamps.

entities.name: Tobias Vale
entities.summary:
*The Pact's spymaster, and the first of the Vales to leave home.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human | Mystic | He/him | Ashen Spire, the Hollow Marches |

**Looks.** A neat man in his late thirties, prematurely grey, in clothes so ordinary they are almost a disguise.

**Manner.** Courteous and dry. Already knows how this conversation ends.

**Who they are**

- Spymaster of the Shadow Pact, in [The Eternal Veil](/player/e/REG-005).
- Of the Vale family, a minor house of Ashen Spire, and the first of the Vales to leave. Brother to [Brother Altharion Vale](/player/e/NPC-020), [Professor Orin Vale](/player/e/NPC-007) and [Sister Elyra Vale](/player/e/NPC-006).

**What people say**

- Tobias Vale wins every fight before it starts.
- He keeps a file on his own family.

entities.name: Tormek Ironheart
entities.summary:
*A dwarven juggernaut in armour he built himself. No blade has pierced it.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dwarf | Artificer | He/him | The Anvil of Dominion, the Tyrant's Dominion |

**Looks.** A stout dwarf almost never seen out of his own armour: black iron plates, riveted and glowing faintly at the seams.

**Manner.** Gruff, practical and endlessly tinkering. Answers questions about his armour in exhausting detail.

**Who they are**

- A dwarven juggernaut of the Crimson Legion, in [The Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003).
- Built his own armour at the Anvil of Dominion.

**What people say**

- No blade has ever pierced his defence.
- He sleeps in the armour.
- He is building a second suit, and nobody knows who it is for.

entities.name: Torren Kell
entities.summary:
*A scavenger captain who wants wealth without allegiance, and avoids the Scar.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Earth Genasi | Rogue | He/him | The Scar, the Hollow Marches |

**Looks.** A rust-coloured earth genasi whose skin is pitted like old iron, in scavenged armour from five armies.

**Manner.** Jokey and mercenary, until someone mentions the Scar.

**Who they are**

- A scavenger captain in [The Hollow Marches](/player/e/REG-001).
- Wants wealth without allegiance.

**What people say**

- His crew will not go near the Scar.
- Ask him why and he changes the subject.

sections.heading: Sea crossing
sections.content: Ships travel across [the Black Tides](/player/e/LOC-902) between [Kaelholm](/player/e/SET-302) and unnamed Eternal Veil ports. The passage takes **about two weeks**. Crew extinguish lanterns over the trench where the Rift runs below the sunless sea. Regular crossings are newly established by campaign start; smugglers also use the route.

sections.heading: Rift crossing [HOMEBREW]
sections.content: [The Rift](/player/e/LOC-901) has an open end in the Hollow Marches and another by [Ashvale](/player/e/SET-301). Travellers can enter one end, cross the Ethereal Realm's border layer, and emerge from the other. The source suggests this route for parties around level 11 and above.

entities.name: Varik "the Bloodforged"
entities.summary:
*A half-orc mercenary lord covered in contract scars. Never lost a duel.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Half-orc | Paladin | He/him | The Bleeding Arena, the Eternal Veil |

**Looks.** A broad half-orc covered in contract scars: a raised line for every oath sworn in blood.

**Manner.** Grand, honourable and theatrical. Keeps every promise to the letter.

**Who they are**

- A mercenary lord of the Bloodbound Company.

**What people say**

- Varik is covered in contract scars.
- Varik has never lost a duel.

entities.name: Varkhaal
entities.summary:
*The Crimson Legion's Iron Citadel, a city of fortresses built around the Great Arena.*

> You hear Varkhaal before you see it: a roar that rises and breaks and rises again from the Great Arena. The city is all iron and red stone, every house a little fortress, every crossroads a duelling ring. Smoke climbs out of the mountainsides around it, where the forges never stop. Soldiers of every people walk the streets in Legion red, and all of them are armed.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Tyrant's Dominion, and the seat of the Crimson Legion. Called the Iron Citadel.
- The warlords meet in the Warlord's Hall. The Legion's chief fortress, the Red Bastion, stands nearby.
- Every dispute is settled by a duel. Anyone can challenge anyone.
- The Great Arena holds a tournament every year, open to anyone. The prize is a warlord's favour.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Great Arena | The heart of the city, and its loudest place. Fights every day, and the yearly tournament. |
| The Warlord's Hall | Where the warlords meet, and where the Warlord sometimes sits. |
| The Gutter | The gladiator pits under the arena, where fighters are made, and broken. Every champion started there. |
| Karrath's Anvil | The Red Victor's shrine. Oaths are sworn with a hammer-blow on the anvil, and oath-breakers are broken on it. |
| The Bellows | Forges cut into the mountainside, smoking day and night. The Anvil of Dominion lies further down. |
| Loser Buys | A soldiers' tavern, named for its only rule. A fight a night, and no hard feelings after. |
| The Rings | A duelling circle at every crossroads. Step inside one and anyone may call you out. |
| The Red Bastion | The Legion's chief fortress, a short march from the city walls. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Warlord Garron Kael](/player/e/NPC-024), when he is not at war, and his heir [Darion Kael](/player/e/NPC-033).
- [General Orana Volkash](/player/e/NPC-025), [Champion Valrik the Undying](/player/e/NPC-026), [Korga Bloodfang](/player/e/NPC-027) and [Velkana Stormclad](/player/e/NPC-031), usually at the arena.
- Fighters from everywhere, come for the tournament.

**Getting around**

| From Varkhaal to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border at the Bloodfields, a week through the iron mountains. |
| The Anvil of Dominion | Under the mountains nearby | Forge-roads, hot and crowded. |

**What people say**

- Anyone can challenge anyone in Varkhaal. Most people only do it once.
- Darion Kael holds quiet dinners with foreigners.
- The tournament draws fighters from every dominion, and some of them are spies.

entities.name: Velkana Stormclad
entities.summary:
*A Stormborn gladiator who fights with blade and lightning.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stormborn | Spellblade | She/her | Born in a thunderstorm over the Fractured Nexus |

**Looks.** A Stormborn woman with blue-grey skin, hair that drifts as if underwater, and eyes that flicker when she is angry.

**Manner.** Showy and theatrical. Plays to the crowd, and the crowd loves her.

**Who they are**

- A Stormborn gladiator of the Crimson Legion, in [The Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003).
- Fights with blade and lightning.

**What people say**

- The arena crowds go quiet when the sky darkens over Velkana's fights.
- The Consortium wants her back. She says she has never been theirs.

entities.name: Vess the Grey
entities.summary:
*A Shadow Pact information broker nobody can describe the same way twice.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reptilian (lizardfolk) | Silent Blade | They/them | Noctis, the Eternal Veil |

**Looks.** A grey-scaled lizardfolk in a grey cloak. Witnesses disagree on height, eye colour and how many teeth showed.

**Manner.** Easy, funny and forgettable. Never sits with their back to a door.

**Who they are**

- A Shadow Pact agent in [The Hollow Marches](/player/e/REG-001).
- Trades in information.

**What people say**

- Nobody agrees on what Vess looks like.
- Vess never sits with their back to a door.
- Someone swears they saw Vess in two places at once.

entities.name: Vexis "the Infernal Architect"
entities.summary:
*A kobold builder who makes fire permanent, and mostly works for pay.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kobold | Artificer | They/them | The Anvil of Dominion, the Tyrant's Dominion |

**Looks.** A rust-red kobold in a leather apron, goggles and singed whiskers, carrying a wand made of furnace parts.

**Manner.** Practical, chatty and bored by sermons.

**Who they are**

- A builder of the Ashen Covenant. Not a zealot.

**What people say**

- Vexis makes fire permanent.
- Vexis only joined because the Covenant pays.

entities.name: Vhalek "the Silent Watcher"
entities.summary:
*A githzerai who never speaks or acts. His eyes show the end of all things.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Githzerai | Monk | He/him | Unknown |

**Looks.** A githzerai in a plain grey robe who sits perfectly still, eyes open, for days at a time.

**Manner.** He never speaks or acts.

**Who they are**

- A figure of the Black Sun.

**What people say**

- Vhalek never speaks or acts.
- Meet his eyes and you will see the end of all things.

entities.name: Warlord Garron Kael
entities.summary:
*The hobgoblin warlord who rules the Crimson Legion from the battlefield.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hobgoblin | Warrior | He/him | Varkhaal, the Tyrant's Dominion |

**Looks.** A heavy-set hobgoblin with a grey-streaked crest of hair and a jaw full of gold teeth, each one taken from a rival.

**Manner.** Jovial, crude and suddenly, terrifyingly violent. Never raises his voice before he raises his fist.

**Who they are**

- Leader of the Crimson Legion, the faction that rules [The Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003).
- Rules from the battlefield, not a throne.

**What people say**

- The Warlord holds the Legion through sheer brutality.
- Kael's heir, [Darion Kael](/player/e/NPC-033), does not share the Warlord's taste for war.
- Every gold tooth has a name, and he will tell you all of them.

entities.name: Yulrath "the Warhound"
entities.summary:
*The bugbear berserker the Company unleashes when it wants terror.*

| People | Calling | Pronouns | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bugbear | Warrior | She/her | The Bloodfang Pit, the Verdant Rebirth |

**Looks.** A huge bugbear in a spiked iron collar, with a chain hanging from it that nobody ever holds.

**Manner.** Calm and sleepy, until she is let loose.

**Who they are**

- A berserker of the Bloodbound Company.

**What people say**

- The Company lets Yulrath off the leash when it wants terror.

entities.name: Yvara Ashborn
entities.summary:
*A fire genasi warrior born under an eclipse.*

**Looks.** A fire genasi with charcoal skin cracked with glowing seams, who fights barefoot and leaves scorched footprints.

entities.name: Zepharyos
entities.summary:
*The Arcane Consortium's City of the Unbound, drifting among the clouds.*

> The city is not on the ground. It is islands of rock and tower drifting in the clouds, joined by bridges that are not always there. Some streets run sideways. One district is upside down, and the people in it seem not to mind. Lightning flickers between the spires and nobody looks up. The air tastes of metal and burnt paper.

**What you know**

- The capital of the Fractured Nexus, and the seat of the Arcane Consortium. Called the City of the Unbound.
- The council sits in the Nexus Spire. The Consortium's chief fortress, the Nexus Collegium, stands nearby.
- Magic here is limitless and unstable. Floating islands and shifting time are normal.

**Places in town**

| Place | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The Nexus Spire | Where the Consortium's council sits, at the one point the whole city turns around. |
| The Nexus Collegium | The Consortium's chief fortress and greatest school. |
| The Drift | Districts on floating islands that rearrange every few nights. Maps sell out daily, and are wrong by evening. |
| The Spans | Bridges of light between the islands. Mostly reliable. |
| The Quodlibet | The great market, named for the old scholars' word for an open debate. Spell components, wands and things with no names, sold by the ounce. Some arrive before they are ordered. |
| Ithiel's Lens | The Many-Eyed's temple and observatory: knowledge, magic and the stars, watched through a thousand lenses. |
| The Antipodes | A district that flipped in some old experiment and stayed that way. Its people do not see the problem. |
| The Keel | The one inn that never moves. Nobody knows how. |

**Who you'll meet**

- [Archmagister Veylan Orithis](/player/e/NPC-034), at the Nexus Spire or the Collegium.
- [Archivist Lissara Wynne](/player/e/NPC-035), [Magister Celith Varis](/player/e/NPC-038), [Sorcerer-King Jorvas Myrr](/player/e/NPC-037), [Pyromancer Elaris Duskbane](/player/e/NPC-040) and [Master Talen Voros](/player/e/NPC-042).
- Students from every people and every dominion.

**Getting around**

| From Zepharyos to | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hollow Refuge | About two weeks | A week to the border, a week through storm country. |
| The Echoing Halls and the Rift of Unmaking | Elsewhere in the Fractured Nexus | Neither is anywhere you want to be. |

**What people say**

- Half of Zepharyos floats because of something the Archmagister did by accident.
- If your island moves while you sleep, you pay rent in the new district.
- Some of the bridges lead somewhere other than the next island.
